**Direct answer:** No. Public evidence cannot establish NVIDIA's exact realized AI-chip market share in 2030. Today is 2026-10-27, so 2030 hasn't happened and no observed 2030 figure exists. Anything published about 2030 is a forecast. Even current share estimates disagree because analysts define the market differently.

**Observed or estimated for the present (not 2030)**
- A Motley Fool piece (April 2026) says NVIDIA "currently accounts for an estimated 85% to 92% share of the AI accelerator market". That is an estimate, and the article gives no methodology.
  https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/22/prediction-this-ai-chip-stock-will-become-the-next/
- Silicon Analysts estimates NVIDIA's revenue share at 87% in 2024 (the peak), 81% in 2025, and 75% projected for 2026. It says these are its own estimates based on public earnings plus TrendForce and TSMC data.
  https://siliconanalysts.com/analysis/nvidia-ai-accelerator-market-share-2024-2026
- The same source says NVIDIA's "floor is likely 65-70% share even in the most competitive scenario." It gives no 2030 figure.
  https://siliconanalysts.com/analysis/nvidia-ai-accelerator-market-share-2024-2026
- Whether hyperscaler custom chips are counted changes the answer. A search summary of 2026 estimates gave a 70–86% revenue-share range. It also cited, second-hand, TrendForce at 27.8% of AI server shipments for custom ASICs (application-specific chips) in 2026. Revenue share and unit share therefore differ.
  https://commandlinux.com/statistics/ai-gpu-market-share-nvidia-vs-amd-vs-intel/ (I did not open this page, so this rests on the search summary only.)

**Projections for 2030 (not outcomes)**
- A scenario analysis in the first search summary has NVIDIA's share compressing from about 80% to 65% by 2030. A separate summary attributes a 70% by 2030 projection to Kearney, and 65–70% by 2028 to Celadon Research. I read none of these pages, so treat these figures as unverified.
  https://celadonresearch.com/research/nvidia-ai-accelerators-q1-2026
- A Motley Fool piece says analysts expect TSMC revenue of about $311.5B by 2030. That figure is about TSMC, not NVIDIA's share, and shows what the 2030 numbers in this area look like: analyst expectations.
  https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/22/prediction-this-ai-chip-stock-will-become-the-next/

**Limits of this research**
- I used about five of the eight allowed retrievals. One of the two pages in my first read returned HTTP 403.
- Most sources are commentary, with single-source support and no audited share data.
- I did not find a primary source such as IDC, Omdia or TrendForce.
- Sibyl flagged that I did not quote the "2025/2026" figures or any 2030 number for claims Q2.C2 and Q2.C3. I did not fix that, so those quotes are weaker than they should be. Q1 (whether any observed 2030 data exists) was only addressed by reasoning from the date, not by a dedicated source.

**Bottom line:** the best supportable statement is that estimates of NVIDIA's share are falling from a peak near 87% in 2024. Forecasts for 2030 sit roughly in the 65–70% range, and those come from secondary sources I did not verify. A realized 2030 figure will only exist after 2030, and it will depend on how the market is defined.

Sources:
- [Motley Fool, April 2026](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/22/prediction-this-ai-chip-stock-will-become-the-next/)
- [Silicon Analysts](https://siliconanalysts.com/analysis/nvidia-ai-accelerator-market-share-2024-2026)
- [Celadon Research](https://celadonresearch.com/research/nvidia-ai-accelerators-q1-2026) (search summary only)
- [Command Linux statistics](https://commandlinux.com/statistics/ai-gpu-market-share-nvidia-vs-amd-vs-intel/) (search summary only)
